function.name: get_air_quality
function.description: Retrieve real-time air quality and pollution data for a specific location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city that you want to get the air quality data for.

detail.description: If true, additional data like PM2.5, PM10, ozone levels, and pollution sources will be retrieved. the value is set to false to default.

historical.description: Optional date (in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format) to retrieve historical data.

They also mention today is 2023-05-05. So we need to call the function get_air_quality with location "New York City", detail true, and historical dates for each of those days. But the function signature only allows one historical date at a time. We might need to call it multiple times? The function returns data for a specific location and date. We can call it three times: for 2023-05-05, 2023-05-04, 2023-05-03. Or maybe we can pass historical as an array? No, it's a string. So we need to call it three times.

We should first call for today: location "New York City", detail true, historical "2023-05-05". Then for yesterday: "2023-05-04". Then for day before yesterday: "2023-05-03".
